President Trump's envoy is calling Russian President Vladimir Putin
a humanitarian after he released an American man
who was captured by Russia in Ukraine.
NPR's Michelle Kellerman reports Trump says he asked Putin
to release Stephen Hubbard, who's now on his way home.
President Trump calls it an amazing thing that Hubbard was released
and he says he gave nothing in exchange.
But the news came soon after Trump made a diesel deal with Russia
and waved sanctions, facing pushback from many in Washington,
including Republicans who say Trump should be putting more pressure on Russia.
If we did what these foolish people wanted me to do,
he wouldn't be coming out right now.
He'd be in there for another 20 years.
So the last thing I was going to do is break up that.
Hubbard, a retired teacher, was living in eastern Ukraine
when Russia invaded and captured him, accusing him of being a mercenary.
The U.S. considered him a hostage.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department.
President Trump said today that criticism of his decision to pause sanctions
on Russia is coming from "people who don't know how life works,"
and he again said that his team is very close to a deal to end the war.
Israeli forces detained New York Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander today
as he helped Palestinian farmers harvest olives in the West Bank.
He was released hours later, but dozens of other volunteers remained in custody.
The Israeli military said the farmers and volunteers failed to seek prior approval
for the harvest, posing a security risk this year's harvest has been marked by violence.
Democrats appear to be making inroads in deep red areas
that have not been competitive in years, places like Kansas, Iowa and Nebraska.
As NPR's Sam Greenglass reports, many of these campaigns are getting inspiration
from a populist movement from more than a century ago.
Prairie populism bloomed across the Great Plains at the end of the 1800s,
and united small farmers and workers against corporate monopolies.
Now candidates in places like Montana, Iowa and Arkansas are embracing it.
Nebraska Democratic Party Chair Jane Klebs says it's frustrating to hear Democrats
say the only way to solidify power in Washington is to restructure elections.
I think instead of these theoretical ivory tower conversations,
we should get back to nuts and bolts organizing in these states.
We used to elect Democrats in Iowa, Nebraska, South Dakota, North Dakota, Montana.
Klebs says Democrats can't just compete in the same battlegrounds every year.
Sam Greenglass, NPR News.
President Trump's political groups have spent more than one quarter of a billion dollars
to bolster Republicans in the final stretch of this year's midterm elections.
It's an unprecedented amount for a sitting president.
Trump's MAGA Inc. PAC has reported spending nearly $277 million
since the beginning of September. That includes major transfers
to two affiliated groups that have been spending millions on advertising.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
North Korea's government will resume broadcasting propaganda
across the heavily armed border with South Korea this month.
The psychological warfare comes after landmine blasts
injured three South Korean front-line soldiers.
South Korea has said North Korean soldiers crossed the military demarcation line
50 times this year while adding landmines, barbed-wire fences, and anti-tank barriers.
New research offers some evidence that psychedelics may fight inflammation
in people with diseases like Parkinson's.
The findings were published in the medical journal JAMA Psychiatry Today,
and Piers Will Stone reports.
It's an area of psychedelic research that hasn't received as much attention,
but experiments in animals consistently show some psychedelics
have powerful anti-inflammatory effects.
Now a team at UCSF has published data from a small study of people with Parkinson's.
They saw markers of inflammation in the blood declined
after they took psilocybin, and that persisted 30 days after.
Dr. Ellen Bradley at UCSF says the findings need to be confirmed in larger trials.
This gives us this initial biological signal to investigate.
People with neurodegenerative conditions are typically excluded from studies on psychedelics,
but Bradley says their finding these substances may actually help symptoms.
Will Stone, NPR News.
Katherine Breed has become the first person to swim the entire length of California's coastline.
She began the journey on July 1st from the California-Oregon border,
finishing about two miles offshore from Tijuana on Monday.
She battled storms, saw a few sharks, and braved to 48-degree waters
during the 100-day long journey.
This is NPR News.
